subject: Velocity scorecard & QBR prep — action grid for latency, cost, uptime, usage
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: sam.harper@ventracloud.com, ops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Velocity scorecard & QBR prep — action grid for latency, cost, uptime, usage

Team — attaching the March velocity scorecard PDF and an initial action grid (spreadsheet attached). High-level items from the dashboard I want us to consider for the QBR and leadership check-in: 

- Latency: p95 rose 18% in Feb on multi-tenant hosted endpoints after the new batching policy. Root cause looks like a burst of short-sequence traffic that bypassed prefix cache.
- Cost: unit cost per 1k tokens increased ~9% (GPU hours vs token growth mismatch). Some of this is due to repeated small requests from a single partner integration (VentraCloud).
- Uptime: 99.92% for the month — two brief incidents (15m and 22m) related to autoscaler misconfig during a patch.
- Usage: active accounts +5% M/M, but median tokens per session down 12% (more short queries).

Immediate asks (QBR focused):
1) Laura — can you validate the p95 attribution by EOD Thu? If the prefix cache miss rate spikes line up, we should propose a canary tweak for batching for the QBR.
2) Vivek — status on autoscaler policy rollback plan? We need a mitigation we can describe in the QBR that reduces incident surface.
3) Marissa — please draft a 90s slide summarizing cost drivers (tokens vs GPU-hours) and include the partner-level breakdown for VentraCloud.
4) Priyom — run a quick sampling eval of short-sequence traffic to see if we can apply lightweight batching client-side; note any UX impact.

I'm looping VentraCloud (Sam) because their integration shows repeated tiny requests that materially affect unit economics; Sam — appreciate any color on roadmap for batching on your side.

Attachments: kpi-velocity-scorecard-2027-03.pdf (dashboard), qbr-action-grid-connor-v1.xlsx (editable)

Thanks — I'll consolidate notes into the action grid after replies.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velocity scorecard & QBR prep — action grid for latency, cost, uptime, usage

Connor — quick check after a brief look at the PDF: I see the p95 increase concentrated in the west region and primarily on the /generate endpoint for sequence lengths < 64. Two immediate notes: 

- Quoted: "p95 rose 18% in Feb on multi-tenant hosted endpoints after the new batching policy."
  * I can confirm the time windows line up with the batching rollout in us-west-2 (Feb 8–10).

- Suggested canary: If we limit continuous batching for short sequences on the multi-tenant pool (retain for dedicated), the client-visible latency for longer sequences shouldn't change and we should recover the p95 for short requests.

Action items for me: I'll export the region breakouts and add a brief appendix showing the sequence-length histogram. I'll also flag three example traces (two from VentraCloud) so we can show a before/after in the QBR. ETA: Thu 17:00 PT.

A couple of practical asks for the QBR slide: can we get a single-row summary that calls out: Net p95 delta, Cost delta, Uptime impact (minutes), and one-line mitigation status? That will help the exec slide.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Observability & Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, sam.harper@ventracloud.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velocity scorecard & QBR prep — action grid for latency, cost, uptime, usage

Connor/Laura — quick update on the autoscaler item: we have a tested rollback that pins the target utilization to the pre-rollout curve and disables aggressive downscale for short windows. It reduces the chance of 1–2 node flapping during patch windows (which caused the 22m incident).

Plan: schedule a constrained canary in us-west-2 on Friday for 6 hours starting 09:00 PT to validate no increased cost impact. If green, we promote the rollback as a mitigation for the QBR narrative and target full rollout Week of Mar 14.

I'll add this to the action grid and tag owners. Wanted to flag that the rollback increases steady-state GPU-hours by ~0.6% in the canary config — worth calling out in the cost slide.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — consolidating next steps below and updating the attached action grid (version 1 -> v1.1):

Decisions and owners:
- Laura: finalize p95 attribution appendix and include two VentraCloud traces (ETA Thu 17:00 PT).
- Vivek: run the constrained canary on Fri 09:00 PT, confirm steady-state delta and incident mitigation; capture cost delta for the slide.
- Marissa: draft the 90s cost slide by Mon EOD and call out VentraCloud as a partner driver; include the 0.6% GPU-hour note.
- Priyom: produce a sampling report for short-sequence traffic and a short ops-runbook for lightweight client batching (ETA Mon 12:00 PT).

External outreach: Sam (VentraCloud) — we appreciate the early visibility. If your team can prioritize a client-side batching change or give us a timeline, please drop it in the shared action grid.

Attachments: qbr-action-grid-connor-v1.1.xlsx (updated with owners/ETAs), kpi-velocity-scorecard-2027-03.pdf (same dashboard)

I'll prepare a one-slide exec summary for Monday's leadership sync and circulate by 11:00. If there are any objections to the canary schedule, flag now.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
